what_it_is:
- rustup installs and updates the toolchain
- cargo new / build / run / check
- Cargo.toml is the manifest; Cargo.lock pins exact versions

- Adds the rand crate from crates.io
- cargo fetches, builds and locks it
- A crate's build script runs on your machine at build time

- Bindings are immutable by default; mut opts in
- Shadowing: let x = …; again makes a new binding, can change type
- const needs a type and a compile-time value

- Integers i8…i128, u8…u128, isize/usize; f32/f64; bool; char
- char is a 4-byte Unicode scalar, not a byte
- Overflowing a literal is a compile error

- fn with typed parameters and -> return type
- Blocks are expressions; the last expression without ; is returned
- A stray ; turns the return value into ()

- // line comments
- /// doc comments become rustdoc (ch 14)

- Each value has one owner; dropped when the owner goes out of scope
- Assigning a non-Copy value moves it; the old name is invalid
- Copy types (i32, bool, char) are copied instead
- Fixes for use-after-move: clone, borrow, or stop using the old name

- &T borrows to read; &mut T borrows to change
- Many & or exactly one &mut, never both at once
- The compiler rejects dangling references

- &str and &[T] are views into data you don't own
- A slice is a pointer plus a length
- String literals are &str

- Named-field structs; tuple structs; unit structs
- Field init shorthand and ..update syntax
- #[derive(Debug)] to print them

- impl blocks attach behaviour to a type
- &self reads, &mut self changes, self consumes
- Associated functions (no self) like Dom::new()

- Each variant can carry its own data
- Option<T> = Some(T) | None replaces null
- Enums model 'one of these shapes'

- Must cover every variant (exhaustive)
- Arms bind the data inside a variant
- _ catches the rest

- if let: handle one pattern, ignore the rest
- let…else: bind or bail out early

- A package has a Cargo.toml and holds crates
- Library crate (lib.rs) vs binary crate (main.rs)

- mod groups code; everything is private by default
- pub exposes it; crate:: and super:: are paths

- use brings a path into scope
- pub use re-exports, shaping a crate's public API

- mod foo; loads foo.rs or foo/mod.rs
- The file tree mirrors the module tree

- Growable, heap-allocated, contiguous
- v[i] panics out of range; v.get(i) returns Option
- Holding a & to an element blocks pushing to the Vec

- String is owned and growable; &str is borrowed
- No s[i]: UTF-8 characters vary in byte length
- Iterate with .chars() or .bytes()

- Key-value store
- entry() API for insert-or-update
- Inserting an owned key moves it into the map

- Unrecoverable error: unwinds and stops the thread
- unwrap() and expect() panic on None or Err

- Result<T, E> = Ok(T) | Err(E)
- ? returns the error to the caller early
- Map errors into your own error enum

- Panic for bugs and broken invariants
- Return Result for bad input

- Type parameters: fn largest<T>(…)
- Compiled to one copy per concrete type (monomorphisation)

- Shared behaviour: impl Trait for Type
- Trait bounds: T: Display
- derive gives Debug, Clone, PartialEq for free

- 'a names how long a reference stays valid
- Usually inferred (elision); written when a function returns a borrow
- A struct holding a & needs a lifetime

- #[test] functions
- assert!, assert_eq!, assert_ne!
- #[should_panic]; tests returning Result

- cargo test runs all; filter by name
- --nocapture shows println! output
- #[ignore] for slow tests

- Unit tests in #[cfg(test)] mod tests, next to the code
- Integration tests in tests/ use only the public API

- Reading arguments and files
- Splitting main.rs from lib.rs
- Errors and test-driven development together

- Anonymous functions that capture their surroundings
- Fn / FnMut / FnOnce depending on how they capture

- Iterator trait: next() -> Option<Item>
- Adapters (map, filter, rev) are lazy until collect() or a loop
- Often as fast as a hand-written loop

- Release profiles
- Publishing and documentation
- cargo install; extending Cargo

- Several crates share one Cargo.lock and target/
- Members listed in the root Cargo.toml

- Owns a value on the heap
- Lets a type contain itself (recursive types)
- Box<dyn Trait> holds any type behind one trait

- Rc: shared ownership, reference-counted, one thread
- RefCell: mutate through & with borrows checked at runtime, panicking on a clash
- Rc<RefCell<Node>> is the classic tree

- Rc cycles never free (a leak)
- Weak<T> points without owning, which breaks the cycle

- Threads; channels for message passing
- Mutex and Arc for shared state
- Send and Sync: which types may cross threads

- Futures and async/await
- An async runtime drives the futures
- Streams

- dyn Trait: dynamic dispatch
- Choose behaviour at runtime

- Destructuring, guards (if), @ bindings
- Where patterns can appear

- unsafe and what it allows
- Advanced traits and types
- Macros

- TcpListener; parsing HTTP by hand
- A thread pool

- Optional, named parts of a crate
- Turned on with --features; can pull in optional dependencies
